data.name: Sereniel
data.gender_notes: Sereniel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'serene', meaning tranquil, calm, and peaceful. In Christian tradition, it can be associated with the serene and calm demeanor of angels or saints. The name Sereniel carries the meaning “Serene, heavenly” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Sereniel usually hope their child will grow to embody serene, heavenly and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that evokes peace, tranquility, and a connection to the divine.
data.etymology: Sereniel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Serene, heavenly.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sereniel total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_latin.name: Sereniel
in_latin.meaning: Nomen pacis, serenum, curatio, et amor
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Sereniel significat vitam pacificam, serenum, curam, et amorem. Auctus ex nomine sancto, Sereniel denotat personam pacificam, serenam, curam, et amorem Dei. In traditione Christiana, Sereniel videtur nomen sanctum, quod significat vitam in pace et amore Dei.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sereniel carries a calming and soothing quality, evoking images of serene, tranquil, and peaceful environments. It is a name that can be given to a child, as a reminder of the importance of inner peace and calmness, especially in our tumultuous and chaotic world. The name can also be used as a nickname or a term of endearment, conveying a sense of calmness and peacefulness.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian spirituality, the name Sereniel carries deep spiritual significance as it represents the calm and peaceful demeanor of angels or saints. Angels are often depicted as serene beings, full of grace and light, and Christians believe that they serve as messengers of God, bringing comfort, hope, and love to those in need. Saints, too, are considered calm and peaceful, even in the face of great suffering and adversity. By adopting this name, one can aspire to embody the serene and calm demeanor of angels and saints, cultivating inner peace and tranquility, and drawing closer to God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sereniel, meaning "heavenly calm," embodies the tranquility and peace that comes from a deep connection with God. This name evokes images of angels in the heavens, serenely watching over the world below, reminding us of the divine presence that brings calmness to our souls.

historical_references.reference: According to medieval legends, Sereniel was a fairy queen who lived in a magical crystal forest. She was reputed to possess the power to heal all ailments, including the most grievous wounds and incurable diseases. Sereniel was believed to be the protector and guardian of the forest, and her presence was invoked for blessings and protection.

Another reference to Sereniel comes from the 16th century book 'The Mirror for Magicians' by Cornelius Agrippa. In this text, Sereniel is mentioned as a powerful angelic spirit, who could be summoned by magicians for various purposes, including invisibility, protection, and the acquisition of treasure.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Sereniel, derived from the Hebrew word 'seren' meaning tranquil or calm, is experiencing a modern resurgence in popularity due to its unique, nature-inspired, and mythological qualities. It is often sought after by parents looking for unconventional baby names that evoke a sense of peace and serenity, and can be found on various platforms such as Pinterest for baby name inspiration, Instagram for name reveal announcements, and Etsy for personalized name products. The name may also be associated with the character Sereniel from the popular fantasy novel 'The Silmarillion' by J.R.R. Tolkien.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Sarah Sereniel in London, United Kingdom credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Sereniel, which means "Serene, heavenly". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
